name: Cave In
label: Hydra Head
lede: Cave In started as metallic hardcore in Methuen, turned toward space rock, signed to RCA, and went back to Hydra Head with the heavy songs the label wouldn't release. Bassist Caleb Scofield died in 2018; the band finished the record he'd played on and kept going.

eras.title: Named after a Codeine song
eras.text: Brodsky and Frechette start the band in Methuen in early 1995. Two years later it has a 7-inch on Aaron Turner's Hydra Head, and the singer leaves mid-tour for another band.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cave In · Wikipedia: Stephen Brodsky
years.h: [[Stephen Brodsky|a0ff602c-7f3e-472d-8786-953da6cd7591]] and Jay Frechette start a band in Methuen
years.p: Frechette sings, [[Adam McGrath|489a27df-e1c7-442d-b25b-067a950b7a5b]] plays second guitar, [[John-Robert Conners|5665286e-b278-4453-9636-c495412a8b24]] drums and Justin Matthes bass. The name is borrowed from the Codeine song Cave-In.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists the original five as Frechette, Brodsky, McGrath, Conners and Matthes, with Andy Kyte briefly replacing Matthes. The Codeine song is on their album Frigid Stars.

Brodsky's first band was a middle-school two-piece called Parasite, with Conners on drums. He later played in Kid Kilowatt with McGrath and [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]]. Before the first 7-inch there were demos and splits with Gambit, Piebald and Early Grace.

years.h: The first official record is a self-titled 7-inch
years.p: It comes out on Hydra Head Records, the label run by [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]] of [[Isis|5e521e8c-0ab2-44c4-8fd8-14d8d3321265]]. The demos and split 7-inches with Gambit, Piebald and Early Grace came before it.

years.h: Frechette quits mid-tour for Ten Yard Fight
years.p: A three-week East Coast run with [[Morning Again|1b4e059e-856e-49a8-b7ca-c3ee67dcde23]] and Bird of Ill Omen is cut short, and Dave Scrod takes over vocals.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls it a mutual decision: Frechette had commitments to the Boston band [[Ten Yard Fight|c051f242-5907-42ce-b25f-678f14323dac]], and he joined it full-time.

eras.title: Scofield arrives, the van doesn't make it
eras.text: A first album in three weeks at God City, with the line-up shifting under it. Brodsky ends up at the microphone, Caleb Scofield picks up the bass, and a Ford Econoline gives out outside Philadelphia.

years.h: Beyond Hypothermia collects the early 7-inches
years.p: The compilation gathers the earlier 7-inch releases and recordings: Cave In on tape before Brodsky became the singer.

years.src: Wikipedia: Caleb Scofield · Wikipedia: Cave In
years.h: A bass player from Pembroke, New Hampshire, auditions
years.p: That's the band's own bio on [[Caleb Scofield|86aa5227-3afb-4198-bf58-9db0946e5d4b]]'s first try-out rehearsal. Dave Scrod had left two weeks before the first-album session, and Brodsky had moved up to lead vocals.
years.xp:
The bio says the band knew Scofield was offering to play bass but not that he could. He had sung in a New Hampshire hardcore band called Strike 3.

He stayed for twenty years, until his death in 2018.

years.h: Kurt Ballou engineers the debut at God City in three weeks
years.p: Recorded April 26 to May 16 in Allston. Ballou's [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] bandmate Jacob Bannon, Jay Randall of Agoraphobic Nosebleed and Travis Shettel of Piebald join him in adding vocals.
years.xp: McGrath cited Cable, Converge and Rorschach as the influences. Brodsky has called the record "Converge worship."

years.h: Until Your Heart Stops arrives as Hydra Head HH666-31
years.p: Fast, dense metallic hardcore, and the first record with Brodsky singing. Loudwire put it on its 2020 list of the top 25 metalcore albums.
years.xp:
Wikipedia calls it a landmark of metallic hardcore. Reviews ran from 10/10 at Blistering to a B+ at Stylus.

Relapse reissued it on March 31, 2023, with remastered tracks, unreleased demos and alternate takes.

years.h: A burning Ford Econoline ends the Isis tour
years.p: The band's 1991 van catches fire at a rest stop about fifty miles from Philadelphia, and the run stops there.

eras.title: Space rock, then a major label
eras.text: Most of the screaming goes and the melodies arrive. Spin tags the band "emo-metal Radiohead," and RCA signs it.

years.h: A five-song EP, Creative Eclipses, points at the sky
years.p: It is the first real sign of the move into space rock, a few months ahead of Jupiter.

years.h: Jupiter drops the screaming, almost
years.p: Brian McTernan produced it in February and March 2000. Big Riff is the only track that still has screamed vocals.
years.xp:
The cover came in four colours across pressings: green first, then magenta, blue and yellow. Pitchfork gave it 4.9, AllMusic 3.5 out of 5 and Brave Words & Bloody Knuckles 8 out of 10. In December 2009 Decibel ranked it the second-best metal album of the decade.

Spin's Sound Advice column tagged the band "emo-metal Radiohead," a label the band rejected. Major labels started calling.

years.h: Methuen to the majors
years.p: Three Hydra Head records in, the band signs with RCA Records in April 2001. Hydra Head stays in the picture, and still releases an EP during the RCA years.

years.h: Three months at Cello Studios, against four days for Jupiter
years.p: Producer Rich Costey and RCA's budget give the band three months in Los Angeles. The whole process ran six months.
years.xp: RCA pressed for radio-friendly singles, and the process had more people in it than the band was used to. Wikipedia says the label's push shaped how the songs were written.

years.h: Tides of Tomorrow keeps Hydra Head in the picture
years.p: A six-song EP on Hydra Head Records, released while the band is signed to RCA, leaning further into melody.

eras.title: Antenna, then the exit
eras.text: A Lollapalooza second stage, a European run behind Foo Fighters and Muse, and older fans telling the band what they think. The heavier songs it writes next are the ones RCA won't release.

years.h: Antenna gives the band its only charting single, Anchor
years.p: The RCA debut is clean vocals and prog and space-rock textures. Alternative Press gave it five stars; Pitchfork gave it 6.1, and Metacritic lands at 78.
years.xp:
Anchor, released May 19, 2003, peaked at 53 on the UK Singles chart and 34 on US Modern Rock. It's the only Cave In song on either. McGrath later called it a poor single choice, though RCA backed it. Inspire followed on August 12, with a video directed by Gavin Bowden.

After the label's merger with BMG and Sony, a scheduled meet-and-greet had no one at it, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Lollapalooza's second stage, then Europe behind Foo Fighters and Muse
years.p: The live set gets heavier as it goes. By September 2003 the band is back in the US with From Autumn to Ashes, Every Time I Die and Funeral for a Friend.

years.big: "We got major backlash for growing out of our metal phase."
q: We were young and naive to the whole process and it affected how we wrote songs.
years.h: Old fans answer Antenna with hostility
years.p: Adam McGrath on the response to Antenna, which turned up at shows as hostility and thrown debris.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports McGrath saying the band received hostile responses, and that the experience pushed it back toward heavier material by September 2003. McGrath also said the major-label years came with a lot of new people around the band.

years.src: Wikipedia: Perfect Pitch Black · Wikipedia: Antenna · Wikipedia: Cave In
years.h: RCA won't release the heavy songs, so the band takes them home
years.p: The split comes in September 2004. RCA returns ownership of the heavier recordings, and the band brings them to Hydra Head.
years.xp: Accounts differ on how it ended. The Perfect Pitch Black page has RCA declining the heavier songs and dropping the band. The Cave In page calls it a mutual agreement, and the Antenna page points to the BMG and Sony merger leaving the band's status uncertain. All three have the band back at Hydra Head.

eras.title: Heavy again, then a long pause
eras.text: A record that takes more than two years to finish, a drummer who moves to Germany, and a hiatus announced in November 2006.

years.h: The heavy songs RCA refused become Perfect Pitch Black
years.p: Recording started in January 2003 with Andrew Schneider, with more work at Translator Audio in Brooklyn in April 2005. It goes back to slow, weird, heavy songs.
years.xp:
PopMatters' Cosmo Lee wrote that it "channels the band's frustration with its major label experience into its most aggressive effort since Jupiter." Pitchfork gave it 7.3, LambGoat and PopMatters 8 out of 10.

Brodsky credited ZZ Top's Tejas, on heavy rotation while touring, for the boogie feel, and the Allman Brothers for the dueling guitars.

years.cap: Cave In at the Backstage Club, Munich
years.h: Conners moves to Germany and Ben Koller steps in
years.p: Conners is injured and relocates to Germany. Koller of [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] takes over drums and plays the record's tours, including a cassette single of Shapeshifter and Dead Already.

years.h: Cave In goes on hiatus
years.p: Touring for Perfect Pitch Black wraps up and the band goes quiet. The break lasts more than three years.

years.h: Pet Genius and Zozobra fill the quiet
years.p: Brodsky and Conners release Pet Genius through Hydra Head. Scofield's sludge band [[Zozobra|a6b8ef30-1d47-4042-9b29-3963e4cd7a7a]] puts out Harmonic Tremors in 2007 and Bird of Prey in 2008.

eras.title: Back at Great Scott's
eras.text: A comeback in Allston, two more records, and a long gap before the next show. Scofield is on bass for all of it.

years.cap: Cave In at Great Scott's, Allston, July 19, 2009
years.h: The comeback is at Great Scott's in Allston
years.p: The band announces in April 2009 that its hiatus is over, then plays July 19. The new songs on the four-song Planets of Old EP debut that night.

years.cap: Cave In in July 2009, the summer of Planets of Old
years.h: Planets of Old goes vinyl first, then CD and DVD
years.p: Hydra Head puts it out on vinyl, then on CD in January 2010 with a DVD of the reunion show. Retina Sees Rewind and Cayman Tongue go up on iTunes.

years.h: White Silence charts at No. 17 on Billboard's Heatseekers
years.p: The band produced it itself. James Plotkin mastered it and [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]] did the artwork.

years.h: Three years without a show, then Doomriders' anniversary
years.p: With no tour announced, Cave In opens Doomriders' tenth anniversary show, its first live date in three years.

years.h: Mutoid Man puts out Bleeder
years.p: Brodsky's band with [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] drummer Ben Koller, formed after Brodsky moved to New York City, releases its debut LP.
years.xp: Brodsky has said he started Mutoid Man with Koller around 2013, per his Wikipedia page.

eras.title: Losing Caleb
eras.text: The bassist of twenty years dies driving home from a writing weekend. The shows that follow raise money for his family.

years.src: Spin: Caleb Scofield obituary · Wikipedia: Caleb Scofield
years.h: Caleb Scofield dies at the Bedford toll plaza
years.p: The 39-year-old's pickup hit a concrete barrier on the Everett Turnpike in New Hampshire, on the drive home from a writing and recording weekend with the band.
years.xp:
A state police official told Spin it appeared he was trying to change lanes just before the plaza. Wikipedia cites the medical examiner as attributing his death to smoke and heat inhalation, thermal injuries and multiple blunt impact injuries. He left his wife, Jen, and two children, aged 7 and 10.

The band's statement: "We are shocked and devastated by the passing of Caleb Scofield. He was one of a kind, our best friend and an unfathomable world of inspiration."

A crowdfunding page for his family passed its $1,000 goal quickly. Spin reported more than $55,000 within days; Wikipedia puts it at about $72,000 within 24 hours.

years.cap: Cave In at the Caleb Scofield benefit, Boston, June 13, 2018
years.src: Wikipedia: Caleb Scofield · Wikipedia: Stephen Brodsky
years.h: Boston plays a benefit for Scofield's family
years.p: Cave In shares the June 13 bill with [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]], Young Widows and a reunited Cancer Conspiracy. Nate Newton, Brodsky and Scofield's brother Kyle cover the bass parts.
years.xp:
A second benefit in Los Angeles on October 13 had Pelican, 27 and Celestial, which was Isis reuniting under another name. Hydra Head put out a fundraising package of Zozobra reissues, unreleased tracks on cassette and an Old Man Gloom tribute shirt.

Brodsky also stood in for Scofield at Old Man Gloom's benefit shows, and became an official member of that band later in 2018.

eras.title: One more record with Caleb
eras.text: The band finishes the four-track demos Scofield played on, then moves to Relapse. Nate Newton takes over the bass for the next record.

years.h: Final Transmission finishes what a four-track started
years.p: Practice-space demos on a handheld four-track, with Scofield on bass, guitar or vocals on all nine tracks. Andrew Schneider mixed it and James Plotkin mastered it.
years.xp:
The title track opens on a voice memo Scofield sent the band, pitching a song idea. The closer, Led to the Wolves, was largely composed by him. Half the proceeds went to his family.

Brodsky: "I don't think I've cried so much putting together any record." McGrath: "Just hearing him play kills me. I'll miss him forever." Metacritic scores it 82.

years.cap: Cave In at the Caleb Scofield benefit, Boston
years.h: The vocals on Shake My Blood get recorded together
years.p: The whole band records them as a group. Kerrang!'s Nick Ruskell calls the album superb on its own terms and wonderful as a tribute.

years.h: Relapse signs Cave In
years.p: The band leaves Hydra Head's folded roster for Relapse, which releases Heavy Pendulum the following May.

years.h: Back at God City, with Nate Newton on bass
years.p: Recorded in January, February and August 2021 at Kurt Ballou's GodCity in Salem, Massachusetts, it's the first full album with Newton. The lead single New Reality carries a riff Scofield wrote in 2011.
years.xp:
Four singles came before the album: New Reality (March 15), Blinded by a Blaze (April 5), Blood Spiller (April 26) and Reckoning (May 10), the first Cave In song written entirely by McGrath. Amaranthine uses lyrics Scofield wrote.

Ballou also engineered the band's debut. The album reached No. 2 on the UK Rock and Metal Albums chart, and Metacritic scores it 81.

years.h: McGrath's solo album is named for the town
years.p: Methuen's Lot takes its name from the town where the band started.
